newsitem.title: USA: Perot fails in lawsuit to join debates.
newsitem.headline: Perot fails in lawsuit to join debates.

text.p: A U.S. federal judge ruled against presidential candidate Ross Perot on Tuesday in his attempt to be included in pre-election debates between President Bill Clinton and Republican challenger Bob Dole.

U.S. District Judge Thomas Hogan turned down a request by Perot, the Reform Party candidate, seeking a restraining order to prevent the debates taking place unless he was included. The first debate is scheduled for Sunday.

The ruling also applied to another minor party candidate, John Hagelin of the Natural Law Party, who, like Perot, had sought a court ruling to stop the debates unless he too was a participant. A lawyer for Perot said there would be an appeal to a federal appeals court.

Lawyers for Perot and Hagelin argued that the Commission on Presidential Debates violated Federal Election Commission rules that state sponors of debates must use "objective" criteria to select debaters.
They said subjective criteria, based on polls and interviews with pundits, to reach the conclusion that only Clinton and Dole had a "realistic chance" of winning the Nov. 5 election.

A lawyer for the bipartisan debate commission, which had recommended only Clinton and Dole as debaters, argued that it had no powers to force anyone to debate. The lawyer said a ruling requiring Perot or Hagelin to debate would jeopardise the debates taking place.
